families.s: HSE COMAH scope, dangerous-substance thresholds and tiering guidance
families.t: dangerous substances, threshold quantities, lower tier, upper tier, inventories, aggregation, applicability review and proportionate duties
f: COMAH applies where dangerous substances are present or are likely to be present at or above specified threshold quantities.
The regulations apply mainly to chemical and storage activities but can also cover explosives, nuclear and other establishments.
Operators should identify substances, classifications and maximum inventories before deciding whether the establishment is lower or upper tier.
Named substances and generic hazard categories must be considered using the applicable aggregation rules.
Lower-tier and upper-tier establishments have different but related duties.
The regulations aim to prevent major accidents and limit consequences to people and the environment.
Applicability should be reviewed when inventories, classifications, processes or establishment boundaries change.
Records supporting the COMAH applicability decision should be clear enough for competent-authority review.
families.g: COMAH applicability depends on the substances, classifications, maximum inventories, aggregation, establishment boundaries, process conditions and current legal thresholds.

families.s: HSE COMAH major-accident-prevention policy and safety-management-system guidance
families.t: MAPP, organisation, hazard evaluation, operational control, management of change, emergency planning, monitoring, audit and review
f: Every COMAH operator must prepare and retain a major accident prevention policy.
The policy should state what the operator intends to achieve in preventing and mitigating major accidents.
The policy should be implemented through a proportionate safety management system.
Organisation and personnel responsibilities are a core element of the management system.
The system should identify and evaluate major hazards and control normal and abnormal operations.
Management of change should cover plant, process, organisation and external changes that can alter major-accident risk.
Emergency planning, performance monitoring, audit and review should be integrated into the system.
Procedures, training records, job descriptions and audit evidence can demonstrate that the policy is implemented.
families.g: MAPP and safety-management-system effectiveness depends on leadership, competence, hazard identification, operational control, change management, emergency readiness, monitoring, audit and corrective action.

families.s: HSE upper-tier COMAH safety-report preparation and assessment guidance
families.t: upper-tier duties, establishment description, dangerous-substance inventory, accident scenarios, prevention, mitigation, safety systems, neighbouring risks and review
f: Upper-tier COMAH operators must prepare and submit a safety report.
The report should demonstrate arrangements for controlling major-accident hazards and limiting consequences.
It should describe the establishment, environment, processes and operating methods.
It should identify dangerous substances and provide relevant classification and inventory information.
Credible major-accident scenarios, causes and conditions should be analysed.
Preventive and mitigation measures, plant safeguards and emergency arrangements should be described.
Neighbouring establishments, external hazards and possible domino effects should be considered.
The report must be reviewed after relevant change, new information or at the prescribed periodic review point.
families.g: Safety-report adequacy depends on complete establishment information, credible scenarios, evidence of prevention and mitigation, management systems, emergency arrangements, external interactions and timely review.

families.s: HSE upper-tier COMAH internal emergency-plan guidance
families.t: written plan, major-accident scenarios, command, communication, resources, evacuation, containment, responders, testing and revision
f: Upper-tier operators must prepare a written internal emergency plan.
The plan should address the full range of foreseeable major-accident scenarios.
Low-probability high-consequence events should not be omitted solely because they are unlikely.
Command, communication and responsibilities should be defined for the initial response and escalation.
The plan should cover warning, evacuation, shelter, rescue, firefighting, containment and environmental protection where relevant.
Equipment, personnel and external support required for the response should be identified.
Information needed by local authorities and emergency services should be supplied promptly.
Plans should be tested, reviewed and revised when exercises, incidents or changes reveal a need.
families.g: Internal emergency-plan effectiveness depends on scenario coverage, command and communication, competent responders, available resources, warning and evacuation, containment, external coordination, testing and revision.

families.s: HSE COMAH public-information and domino-effect cooperation guidance
families.t: public information, affected people, electronic access, upper-tier information, neighbouring sites, domino groups, shared hazards and emergency communication
f: Basic public information is required for every COMAH establishment.
Upper-tier establishments must provide additional information about major-accident hazards and response.
People who could be affected should receive specified information without having to request it.
Public information should be accurate, understandable and updated after relevant change.
The competent authority provides electronic access to establishment information.
Operators in a domino group must cooperate and share information relevant to major-accident risk.
Cooperation can extend to neighbouring sites outside COMAH where they can increase risk or consequences.
Emergency-planning and public-warning arrangements should reflect shared or interacting hazards.
families.g: Public and domino-risk communication depends on current establishment data, understandable hazard information, affected populations, neighbouring activities, shared scenarios, warning methods and update controls.
